resources.string: Simple Browser
Web crawler · secondary source

Defaults: 100 pages, 10,000 queued URLs, 30 minutes total, 16 MiB per page, a 1-second request interval, 3 same-origin redirect hops, and 512 KiB for robots.txt. All are configurable. Set page/queue/duration/body/redirect/robots bytes to 0 for Unlimited. The default application-added HTTP 429/503 wait is 30 seconds and can be set to 0; server Retry-After is still honored. Crawling is explicitly started by you, stays in the foreground, and sends requests serially. It does not crawl in the background, flood with concurrent requests, or create automatic retry storms. It parses only static HTML/plain text actually returned by the server, does not run JavaScript, and does not attach browser cookies, login state, or web sessions. Unlimited body/queue/robots responses may exhaust memory, trigger ANR, or crash the app.

robots.txt is respected by default; you can ask for each disallowed path or ignore it. Whether to follow cross-site destinations and how to handle ordinary non-success HTTP responses are user choices, with explicit prompts where needed. robots.txt is not authorization, and public readability does not mean site rules permit crawling, copying, or republication. For CAPTCHA, login, or paywall signals, you may display only static text actually returned by the server, or stop and open the page manually; the crawler will not submit forms, solve challenges, or bypass access controls. It does not use browser cookies/login state, so authenticated content cannot be fetched. Each 429/503 retry requires your individual confirmation. The application-added wait can be 0, but server Retry-After and your request interval are still honored. No proxy, IP rotation, fingerprint spoofing, or CAPTCHA solving is used.

Network boundary: this crawler uses Android Java HTTP(S) connections and system name resolution. It does not inherit GeckoView\'s Quad9 TRR-only setting and is not guaranteed to pass through the optional DNS-only VPN. Local/private addresses are rejected, but DNS preflight and connection behavior are platform-dependent; do not treat this as the browser\'s DNS privacy protection.

Risk: setting page count, queue, duration, per-page bytes, same-origin redirect hops, or robots.txt bytes to 0 removes that application-configured cap. Android/Java heap, array/string indexing, system allocation, network timeouts, and redirect-loop detection remain technical boundaries. Unlimited reads/crawls may exhaust memory, trigger ANR, or crash. Short delays, a 0 application-added 429/503 wait, or ignoring robots may generate substantial traffic, be rejected/blocked, or violate site rules. A warning appears before every run. This notice reminds you of risks; it does not change legal responsibility or authorization status.

The crawler sends serial requests to the listed site and cross-site destinations you approve. Unlimited pages/queue/body/duration/same-origin redirects/robots.txt reads, short request intervals, a 0 application-added 429/503 wait, or ignoring robots.txt may create substantial traffic, be rejected or blocked, violate site terms, burden third parties, or exhaust Android/Java memory and trigger ANR/crash. Redirect-loop detection still stops repeated URIs; a 0 wait does not skip server Retry-After. Check authorization, site rules, privacy, and service impact. CAPTCHA/login/paywall controls are not bypassed; authenticated content cannot be fetched. Continuing applies your choices to this run only. This notice reminds you of risks; it does not change legal responsibility or authorization status.

Privilege/environment findings for this launch (warnings only; they do not block startup):

Simple Browser v0.6 relaxes some blocking policies from v0.5. Permission, AppOp, process-capability, and environment checks are still reported; non-fatal findings alone no longer block startup. Actual crashes or inability to initialize safely still fail normally.

Developer debugging: USB/ADB DevTools is available by default. The in-app Console can show console argument values, error/rejection text, and stack/path from the active top-level page. Text may contain sensitive data, credentials, or personal information. Connect only trusted devices; turn features off in Settings. Row count, per-entry text/argument size, and event rate offer finite choices or Unlimited; unlimited logging may exhaust memory, trigger ANR, or crash. Data stays in memory and is erased when cleared/closed. No additional cookies, DOM, forms, request/response bodies, or wall-clock time are read; no general JavaScript bridge or native eval is added. Extension installation still explains its all-sites host permission.

Crawler: page count, queue, total duration, per-page and robots.txt body bytes, same-origin redirect hops, request interval, robots policy, and application-added 429/503 wait are configurable; 0 means Unlimited where offered. Java/Android memory, array/string size, system allocation, and network timeouts remain technical boundaries. Unlimited operations may exhaust memory, trigger ANR/crash, cause substantial traffic, rejection/blocking, terms violations, or third-party load. Crawling is explicitly user-started, foreground, and serial. Every 429/503 retry needs confirmation and still honors server Retry-After. CAPTCHA/login/paywall responses may only be shown as actual static server text or opened manually; browser cookies/login state are not shared, so authenticated content cannot be fetched.

Compatibility and rollback: existing v0.5 browser profile, history, bookmarks, and site permissions are retained; relaxed defaults apply in existing profiles and this notice is shown. Disable debugging/Console, adjust crawler options, or exit in Settings. Back up important data before rollback; Android generally does not allow downgrading over a newer install, and uninstalling deletes private app data.

This notice reminds you of risks; it does not change legal responsibility or authorization status.

USB/ADB DevTools is enabled by default (GeckoView still controls endpoint creation through its API). A connected debugger may inspect and manipulate page content; connect only trusted devices. This does not enable Wi-Fi/LAN listening or add Android permissions. Turn it off in Settings.

GeckoView reads this setting when the Runtime is created. Changing it restarts the browser engine and restores open tab URLs; each tab\'s back/forward history resets. Closing the old Runtime also closes its debugging endpoint.

The bundled WebExtension is installed only when you open the current tab Console panel; installation clearly explains and asks for host permission to all HTTP/HTTPS sites. Capture is limited to the selected GeckoSession top-level page while the panel is open. It displays console.log/warn/error argument values and JavaScript error/rejection text plus stack/path; strings may contain credentials or personal information. Ordinary objects and DOM are not expanded. It does not additionally read cookies, forms, request/response bodies, page URLs, or wall-clock time. Row count, per-entry text/argument size, and events per second can be finite or Unlimited; unlimited choices may exhaust memory, trigger ANR, or crash. Data is memory-only, never persisted or uploaded. Pages can forge log entries.

Opening or closing the panel restarts the Gecko Runtime; open tab URLs are restored, but back/forward history and temporary page state reset. When closed, capture stops, the buffer is cleared, GeckoSessions are closed, the extension is uninstalled, and the native message delegate is removed. The preference alone does not start debugging.
